label: Highly connected but emotionally strained heavy social-media users
summary: This profile is characterized by comparatively higher loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms alongside heavier daily social-media use. Respondents in this group appear to combine intensive social-media engagement with elevated emotional distress indicators.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, educated to graduate level or above, and reporting more than 5 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Uses social media heavily on a daily basis
Shows comparatively higher depressive symptom levels
Shows comparatively higher anxiety symptom levels
Represents a medium-sized subgroup in the training sample
tone: Emotionally burdened, digitally immersed, and socially connected yet isolated

label: Low-distress light social-media user
summary: Respondents in this profile show relatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and very low anxiety symptoms, alongside comparatively light daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Typically male, educated to graduate level or above, and reporting about 1–3 hours of social-media use per day.
behavior_markers: Reports relatively low loneliness on the UCLA-8 measure.
Shows low depressive symptom levels on the PHQ-9.
Shows very low anxiety symptom levels on the GAD-7.
Uses social media lightly compared with heavier-use profiles, centered around roughly 1–3 hours daily.
tone: Stable, low-distress, and moderately digitally engaged.

label: Socially Engaged but Lonely Heavy User
summary: This profile shows comparatively higher loneliness alongside lower average depressive and anxiety symptoms, with heavier daily social-media use. It suggests respondents who spend substantial time on social platforms while reporting emotional isolation more than broader mood or anxiety difficulties.
demographic_anchor: Typically represented by a female respondent with graduate-level education or above who uses social media about 3-5 hours per day.
behavior_markers: Uses social media heavily on a daily basis, with average use near 4.9 hours per day
Reports higher loneliness relative to other measured symptoms
Shows lower average depressive symptoms on PHQ-9
Shows lower average anxiety symptoms on GAD-7
May appear digitally connected while still experiencing interpersonal or emotional disconnection
tone: Connected online, but emotionally somewhat isolated; active, functional, and not strongly marked by depression or anxiety.

label: Low-distress, light social-media use graduate man
summary: This profile reflects respondents with comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and low anxiety symptoms, alongside lighter daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Male respondents with graduate-level education or higher who typically report about 1–3 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports relatively low loneliness on the UCLA-8 measure
Shows relatively low depressive symptom levels on the PHQ-9
Shows relatively low anxiety symptom levels on the GAD-7
Uses social media for a lighter amount of time each day compared with heavier-use profiles
Typical daily social-media use centers around roughly 1.6 hours
tone: Generally steady, low-distress, and moderate in daily digital engagement.
